tech.title: Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes
tech.summary: The release notes for Tesla's Full Self-Driving v15 read like a list of the feature's biggest current weaknesses. The update includes improvements to sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones. It also adds an impressive-looking live visualization. FSD can now slow down for speed cameras. The update is currently being rolled out.

tech.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says AI Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math
tech.summary: An Anthropic researcher claims he worked with AI to discover a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The conjecture in number theory predicts how primes are distributed. Mathematicians have been trying to crack it for 167 years, without success. The researcher's proof passed verification with proof-checking software.

tech.title: The Merge
tech.summary: Neuralink has increased the rate of surgeries and extended its clinical trials to Canada and the UK. The first participants in the company's studies now hold video chats with new participants to coach them on how to adjust to the technology. The terms of their trials don't include the option for upgrades. Unless Neuralink comes up with a commercial device, they will have to return to their pre-cyborg lives.

tech.title: AI x Bio is not _just_ a data problem
tech.summary: How far AI gets in biology will depend largely on how much data we have. It will also depend on what is measured and the quality of that data. An abundance of systematically incomplete measurements is unlikely to lead to a comprehensive understanding of many of the complex systems that occur in biology. AI will likely become a powerful tool that will contribute to the study of biology, but there is still no clear path to documenting a comprehensive account of how a whole cell or tissue works.

tech.title: Outcomes are the new experience
tech.summary: Customers don't care ultimately how quickly their questions are answered. What matters is whether or not they got the outcome they needed. Zendesk's Outcome AI Platform is how industry leading brands are winning the future of customer service. Explore Zendesk AI Explore Zendesk Outcome AI

tech.title: Vibecoding an inference chip
tech.summary: AI allows developers to work in entirely new domains by giving them access to new programming languages and paradigms. This developer vibe-coded an FPGA into running an LLM. The article details the experience. The experiment shows what is now possible with a large token budget and interesting problems to point them at.

tech.title: Informal Verification
tech.summary: Verification is an exercise in building trust. A formal approach may be sufficient, but not necessary. This post explores the use of System One models as informal proof checkers. Informal methods can play a complementary role in establishing trust in agentic software engineering flows.

tech.title: I don't expect superintelligence in 2027
tech.summary: The industry seems to have a preference towards believing in extremely short timelines. We are probably about 60% of the way towards superintelligence relative to where we were in 2022. Superintelligence will likely arrive in 2029 rather than in 2027. While this seems like a tiny difference, it changes what the industry should prioritize. The current push towards deprioritizing 'long-timeline' work is not a good idea.

tech.title: The Alice Huang Associate Accused of Funneling Nvidia Chips to China
tech.summary: Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national, was reportedly a central operator of a web of companies that smuggled restricted Nvidia AI chips to China. The web included Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company led by Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang had an affair. Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, living in a luxury villa down the street from the Chinese embassy. Li was charged with fraud in February 2025 in a case tied to the alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. His criminal case is ongoing.

webdev.title: Streaming LLM Responses Without Rendering Every Token
webdev.summary: Give your streaming relay explicit completion and error events, and abort upstream generation when the client disconnects. Buffer incoming tokens and render at most once per animation frame so the browser can keep up.

webdev.title: SwiftUI Doesn't Have a List. It Wraps Someone Else's
webdev.summary: Runtime inspection found that SwiftUI's List wraps NSOutlineView on macOS and UICollectionView on iPhone and iPad. SwiftUI still computes its own diffs and hosts each row in a SwiftUI view, so using the same underlying container leaves room for different update costs.

webdev.title: Your AI Agent Remembers Everything. That's the Problem
webdev.summary: Persistent memory can feed stale facts back to an agent after circumstances change. This piece covers background passes that review and rewrite stored memories and asks how systems should handle corrections, forgetting, and portability.

webdev.title: Superintelligence Is Arriving
webdev.summary: A reported AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis is a sign that superintelligence is approaching. The industry should build AI that expands human agency and keeps people in control.

webdev.summary: Open by telling readers who needs to pay attention so everyone else can move on. In Slack or Teams, put the essentials in the first three to five lines and leave the details in the thread.

webdev.title: It's a Plan
webdev.summary: It's a Plan is a self-hosted issue tracker where teams can assign work to AI agents alongside human teammates. Agents have their own roles and permissions, and an assignment, mention, or schedule can start a run.

webdev.title: I Analyzed the AI Stack Used by 40,000+ Companies
webdev.summary: An analysis of vendor disclosures found that 44.8% of companies naming an AI model provider listed at least two. Anthropic and OpenAI led the counts, while routers grew fastest over the month studied, driven mainly by OpenRouter.

webdev.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
webdev.summary: OpenAI reports that log perplexity on its held-out dataset fell from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to 0.91 for GPT-4. It proposes using perplexity alongside other measures to set shared safety thresholds, while acknowledging that different evaluation datasets make cross-lab comparisons difficult.

webdev.title: Teaching a Web Page to Read a Chess Board
webdev.summary: This browser demo reconstructs a chess position from a screenshot in about a quarter of a second using a 131 KB model and plain JavaScript. Inference stays on the device. The system is designed for flat screenshots and diagrams.

webdev.title: Foxit: 10 PDF MCP Servers for AI Agents, Compared
webdev.summary: Local servers, cloud APIs and self-hosted toolkits handle agent PDF work differently. See what each one reads, modifies and charges for. Read the comparison.

webdev.title: Pattern Engineering
webdev.summary: Engineering teams can make coding agents more reliable by turning recurring workflows into reusable patterns and giving agents ways to verify their work.

webdev.title: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
webdev.summary: Set up Unsloth Desktop on Windows, pick a quantized Inkling or Qwen model that leaves enough GPU memory for your context window, and share it over your home network.

webdev.title: What We Learned Operating Auth for 1,000+ APIs
webdev.summary: After a bug discarded newly rotated OAuth refresh tokens and forced users to reconnect, Nango began saving replacement tokens immediately and allowing only one refresh at a time per connection.

webdev.title: A Short History of Read Streams in Postgres
webdev.summary: Postgres read streams combine adjacent disk pages into a single read, but a page already in shared buffers can split the range into two requests.

devops.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
devops.summary: Google is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to help run AI agents securely at scale. Agent Substrate separates agent state from compute in pre-warmed Kubernetes pools, which Google says lets agents resume in under 500 milliseconds.

devops.title: Introducing in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2
devops.summary: Google Cloud released in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2 in preview for VPC native clusters on GKE 1.35 or later. Teams can move from Dataplane V1 without building a parallel cluster, and they can roll back before finalization.

devops.title: Karpenter v1.15: GPU-aware provisioning, smarter node repair, and more
devops.summary: Karpenter v1.15 adds Dynamic Resource Allocation support to factor GPU topology and networking into provisioning decisions. It classifies node repair as a voluntary disruption that respects Pod Disruption Budgets. The update also introduces a pod deletion cost controller and CEL support for dynamic kubelet configurations.

devops.title: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week
devops.summary: An engineering lead shipped 170 pull requests in a single week by optimizing development loops with AI tooling. Key steps included modernizing CI/CD, moving issue management from Jira to Linear, and building a cloud harness to run orchestrated agents. These changes addressed bottlenecks like slow approvals and inaccurate documentation in the knowledge base.

devops.title: Building PlanetScale with Insights Agent
devops.summary: PlanetScale's database optimization agent added an index that made a production query slower because its SQL summary hid a 645-element IN list. Removing that list and filtering the small result set in Ruby cut average query time from 28.5 milliseconds to 1.95 milliseconds. Another change reordered a feature flag check, reducing database lookups from 28.7 million to 8.3 million per day.

devops.summary: AWS authors propose an observability framework for agentic applications that crosses four layers with three concerns: reliability, cost, and security. They recommend OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and evaluation gates, arguing that agents rarely fail with errors and often return confident wrong answers.

devops.title: The layer of your platform nobody owns
devops.summary: Platform teams standardize nearly everything except the operating system under their clusters. Developers should use an immutable, API-managed OS such as Talos Linux, with declarative configuration and atomic upgrades, at the cost of losing interactive shell access.

data.title: Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story (40 minute video)
data.summary: Booking.com's platform story is less about flashy AI than repeated infrastructure rewrites to remove scaling bottlenecks across data, experimentation, and serving. The company now runs hundreds of models and hundreds of billions of daily predictions, but one standout lesson is operational: lineage plus a delete-first migration strategy let it retire most legacy workflows before cutover, sharply reducing migration risk.

data.title: Self-service agentic analytics at Mews, Part I: data foundations
data.summary: Nearly 500 Mews employees used AI agents to answer their own data questions in the first month, bypassing the analyst ticket queue. The agents use shared metric definitions across tools like Claude, Hex, and Slack, and flag answers that rely on uncertified data.

data.title: How we scaled metrics aggregation by moving durable state into storage
data.summary: At Datadog, recovering aggregation state had become the limiting factor for scaling metrics processing. The system moved from static worker ownership to dynamically reassigned RocksDB state backed by blob storage, to a design where time-series storage reconciles partial aggregates, late arrivals, and duplicates. Keeping historical state out of the streaming recovery path lets workers resume at the live edge, but shifts reconciliation complexity into storage and query paths.

data.title: When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone?
data.summary: Teams building AI features want to ship on offline evals alone and skip slow A/B tests. Spotify shows that works only under strong assumptions that are hard to verify and can change. Noise also hides the link: in the worked example, a naive estimate says the eval explains 24% of online variation, when the true figure is 60%.

data.title: When a Lakehouse Fails: Rebuilding Data Integrity and Pipeline Trust
data.summary: Two IEEE papers focus on a core data-platform problem: how to make lakehouse pipelines recover reliably and remain trustworthy under failure. One emphasizes resilient architecture and replay integrity, while the other explores metadata-driven, AI-assisted ETL with self-repair. Automation only works when recovery, governance, and validation are demonstrably reproducible at scale.

data.title: The data engineering autonomy moment: agents now build and run dlt pipelines, and ingestion becomes a 40x bigger market
data.summary: AI coding agents can now build, run, and fix dlt data pipelines with little human input, and Claude Code started 92% of agent-run pipelines in October. dltHub tracked about 28,000 distinct custom data sources in use, compared with roughly 700 connectors in a typical catalog.

data.title: OpenMetadata 2.1 Makes Semantic Context an Open-Source Platform Concern
data.summary: OpenMetadata 2.1 turns the open-source catalog into more of a semantic context layer: it imports metric definitions from warehouses and BI tools, adds hierarchies and finer-grained lineage, and exposes an RDF knowledge graph through MCP.

data.title: PostgreSQL 19: less friction, more control
data.summary: This interactive tour runs each new PostgreSQL 19 feature on a real Postgres 19 server in a disposable sandbox. It covers IGNORE NULLS, get-or-create inserts, JSON export, JSONPath transformations, and range subtraction, plus planner advice and live logical and physical replication experiments.

data.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released!
data.summary: PostgreSQL 19 lets teams reclaim disk space without blocking reads or writes and gives them more control over query plans. It also makes it easier to enable logical replication without a restart, read recent writes from standby servers, and get or create a row in a single query.

data.title: Introducing Grafana Notebooks
data.summary: Grafana Notebooks bring charts, queries, and findings from Grafana Assistant into one shareable working document. Instead of collecting screenshots and query links to explain an incident, an analyst can show a teammate what supports a conclusion. The document also shows where an assumption is still being made.

data.title: Your biggest tenant runs someone else's plan
data.summary: Prepared statements can push PostgreSQL toward a generic execution plan that fits the average tenant but performs badly for outliers. For example, a large tenant triggered far more work and slower queries than a custom plan. You should observe multi-tenant skew closely and consider forcing custom plans or redesigning indexes and query shapes.

data.title: Project Chaperone: A Rule-Enforcing Harness for Proactive Assessment and Prevention of AI Agent Misconduct
data.summary: Project Chaperone is an open-source harness for constraining AI agents with explicit policy checks before and during execution, rather than relying on prompts alone. It models data-flow, action, output, and network rules so risky operations can be blocked while safe workflows still run. Practical agent safety needs enforceable runtime boundaries, not just instructions.

data.summary: Zerodha's Kite trading platform, with about 20 million customers, stores layouts and UI preferences as JSON blobs, and writes are half its traffic.

marketing.title: How to Build More Buyable B2B Brands
marketing.summary: B2B campaigns that build relatability help buying groups feel more confident defending their purchasing decisions internally. Campaigns with strong buyability signals were 1.7X more likely to qualify as “Strategic Assets”, the highest rung of WARC's B2B Effectiveness Ladder, reserved for campaigns that drive sustained commercial growth. Yet 52% of campaigns featured only one or none of the 3 signals: recommendations, relationships, and relatability. Customer testimonials and use cases appeared in 64% of high-buyability campaigns versus 16% of lower-buyability campaigns.

marketing.title: Why Gen Z Isn't Fully Locked Into Their Job ‘Situationship'
marketing.summary: Gen Z is increasingly reluctant to commit to employers as layoffs and AI-driven job disruption weaken trust in job security. More than 30% of workers could see at least half their job tasks disrupted by generative AI. Meanwhile, 85% could see at least 10% of their tasks affected. This uncertainty makes exploring other opportunities more appealing. However, staying detached can limit career growth by weakening workplace relationships and access to promotions.

marketing.title: 40% of Arcade's Signups Come From AI Search. Here's Their Playbook
marketing.summary: Arcade is an AI video platform for marketers. It drives growth through 3 channels, with AI search generating 40% of signups. It hired a dedicated growth engineer to own AI visibility after an agency underperformed. Founder-led social contributes 20% through recorded interviews turned into a content calendar. Referrals drive another 15% through product features like invite flows and video watermarks. It also asks new users how they discovered the product and runs blind tests against competitors.

marketing.title: Framework for building product messaging from scratch
marketing.summary: Start with an AI-free brain dump based on product knowledge and stakeholder conversations, then review internal call transcripts to identify key messages, value propositions, and features. Translate the messaging into a product page wireframe to test clarity before gathering team feedback. Launch a first version and refine it based on customer responses. This post provides a positioning template to use for future messaging projects.

marketing.title: LinkedIn's Connections Export is Shrinking in December. How Much of Your Network Goes With You?
marketing.summary: Starting in December, LinkedIn will remove connections' email addresses and current companies and job titles from account downloads. Members will still be able to view this information on individual profiles. This makes it harder for companies to transfer a founder's network into sales and marketing databases or keep contact records updated outside LinkedIn.

marketing.title: I Built a Competitor Price Tracker for Black Friday and Cyber Monday
marketing.summary: This piece provides a copy-and-paste AI prompt to build a competitor price tracker. Fill in 8 fields about the company and its competitors. AI monitors public pricing pages and records price changes and promotions. It creates a shared document with price comparisons and change history. A scheduled task keeps the tracker updated daily or weekly.

marketing.title: The Link Building Industrial Complex is Dying
marketing.summary: Traditional link building is losing value as brands question buying backlinks based on domain rating rather than relevance and credibility. AI search requires more than backlinks or brand mentions, since being cited doesn't guarantee a product recommendation. B2B brands may get more value from visibility on review sites like G2 and Gartner than from paid guest posts. Podcasts, influential publications, and videos answering buyer questions are stronger ways to build credibility and earn relevant links.

marketing.title: Deleting blog posts hurt AI visibility, but organic clicks told a different story
marketing.summary: AI visibility scores track how often a brand appears in AI answers, not whether those answers send anyone to the site. Blog posts tend to drive that exposure while service pages drive the clicks, so pruning the blog can sink AI reports as organic clicks hold or rise. Tracker data is also unstable, since answers change on nearly every run and the tested prompts aren't real searches. The solution is to compare Search Console's AI impressions with clicks to the same pages, and to add a “How did you hear about us?” field to inquiry forms.

marketing.summary: Bending Spoons added Mailchimp to its portfolio after also acquiring AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable, and Miro this year.

marketing.summary: Google made its AI-first desktop homepage official, swapping the Search button for AI tools and adding a sidebar of recent AI Mode chats for signed-in users.

marketing.summary: Make bold claims more believable by providing specific examples that address buyer skepticism.
